first look at some of the new robots.
The latest additions to Google's burgeoning robotics empire are a pair of software companies. Boston Dynamics, which makes robot arms, backs a number of companies, including the MIT Open Courseware, which provides free video lectures.
The other purchase is of DeepMind, a British artificial intelligence company that has been working with Google. The search giant has been using DeepMind to improve machine learning, which is the technique that enables self-driving cars to learn to recognize images and objects.
Here's a closer look at the newest members of Google's robotics team:
Boston Dynamics
Boston Dynamics' first robot was named Spot, a four-legged robot designed for surveillance and research. Spot was unveiled in June at Google I/O, the company's annual developer conference.
Spot can run on many types of surfaces and has "very high persistence of vision," according to Boston Dynamics, allowing it to see about 1,000 times better than humans can.

But police and military officials now appear to be retreating from their campaign against drug cartels after the government announced that it was ending the military operation in the area, leaving the area largely in the hands of a loose collection of vigilantes.

They are sounds that echo through the forests of this part of Europe, where they are still made by hand, and they are being revived in a country that is so intent on preserving its traditional crafts that it offers subsidies for people who study them.

The wood-sawing tradition is as old as Poland itself, and it has been practiced by many different ethnic groups who have inhabited the country over the centuries.

Traditional sawyers are old-timers who often have a few years of apprenticeship under their belts — a lifetime in this rural landscape, where the closest thing to an entertainment is a long, leisurely meal on the terrace of a country inn.
